title: PRD: Microlane Behavior Gates and Incremental Launch Checklist
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a per-microlane behavior gating system for the hosted inference surface to enable incremental behavior changes, targeted experiments, and safer rollouts for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank endpoints. This PRD details scope, acceptance criteria, rollout checklist, telemetry requirements, and operational runbooks.
problem_statement: Large behavior changes (model prompt updates, sampling tweaks, deterministic post-processing) currently require full endpoint version toggles or heavy-weight feature flags. That makes rollouts risky, slow, and hard to A/B for quality and cost. We need a lightweight, observable mechanism to gate behavioral changes at micro-lane granularity with deterministic evaluation and automated rollback hooks.
goals: Enable per-microlane behavior flags (called microlane gates) for hosted endpoints so product teams can toggle small behavioral changes without redeploying model variants
Provide deterministic acceptance checks (quality + latency + cost) before widening rollouts
Ship a launch checklist and operational runbook so SRE/Owners can perform safe canaries and automated rollbacks
Expose telemetry and dashboards for gate-level metrics (query-level quality, latency P99, token cost delta)
non_goals: Not building a general-purpose feature-flag service — integrate with existing flags and runtime routing only
Not changing the underlying model compilation/kernels — microlane gates operate at routing and prompt/postprocess layers
Not replacing Dedicated capacity billing or tenancy controls
success_metrics: Fraction of behavioral rollouts performed via microlane gates vs full endpoint version toggles >= 50% within 3 months of launch
Reduction in mean time to rollback for behavioral regressions from >3 hours to <30 minutes
No customer-visible increase in error rate or 99th percentile latency attributable to gates during staged rollouts
At least 3 independent product teams complete a gated rollout and sign acceptance within the first 6 weeks
acceptance_criteria: Gate definitions: YAML manifest format for microlane gates accepted by runtime and validated by console
Operator UX: Console UI to create/target gates with tenant, fraction, and traffic-slice selectors — end-to-end flow validated in staging
API: REST endpoints to create/list/update/delete gates and to attach gates to endpoint routes; swagger docs present
Deterministic evals: Built-in test harness to run a pre-defined eval set per gate producing quality delta, latency distribution, and token-cost delta
Telemetry: Gate-level metrics emitted to observability pipeline (Prometheus + traces + cost breakdowns) with dashboard templates
Rollback hooks: Circuit-breaker policy that auto-rolls back gate if configured thresholds exceeded (quality regression or latency/cost spikes)
SRE runbook: Playbook tested in canary including steps for manual abort, log queries, and follow-up postmortem template
Security: Audit logs at gate change granularity and RBAC controls for gate creation/modification
Performance: Gate evaluation adds <3ms median overhead on warm requests and does not increase P99 by more than 2% on heavy traffic
Integration tests: End-to-end tests in CI exercising creation, canary traffic, detection of regression, and automated rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha (platform teams only) for 2 weeks — validate UI, API, and deterministic evals. Phase 2: Customer pilot with 2-3 low-traffic tenants for 4 weeks with close telemetry review. Phase 3: Gradual opt-in for product teams, enable self-serve gates in Console. Phase 4: Open to all tenants with monitoring guardrails and optional SRE approval for high-impact gates.
checklist_items: PRD review and sign-off from Product, Eng, Design, SRE and Security
Design spec: console flows and API contract published (Confluence link)
Runtime: gate manifest parser implemented and validated in staging
API: endpoints implemented and documented; SDK updates for gate management
Evals: canonical eval set created per endpoint type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
Telemetry: dashboards created and alerted thresholds configured
Canary automation: scripts to drive traffic slices and measure metrics
Rollback automation: circuit-breaker policy implemented and tested in fault-injection lab
SRE runbook written and validated in a dry-run
Docs: admin guide and customer-facing docs drafted and reviewed
Legal/Privacy: review of audit logs and data retention for gate artifacts
Launch comms: internal announcement, migration notes, and support triage plan
decisions: Use a lightweight YAML manifest for gate configuration rather than a database-first UI to simplify code paths and support Git-like audits — decided 2026-03-05
Gates operate at the routing/prompt layer (not kernel or compilation) to reduce risk and keep behavior reversible — decided 2026-03-03
Default canary fraction set to 1% for customer pilots; SRE can override per-gate — agreed 2026-03-07
open_questions: How should we charge for gated rollouts that materially change token cost? (billing products input requested)
Do we need tenant-level guardrails for simultaneous gates to avoid combinatorial risk? (security/SRE to propose limits)
Should the deterministic eval harness live in a central repo or per-team eval repos? (tradeoff: discoverability vs autonomy)
